questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number.

32 : 99 : : ? : 45 : : 16 : 51
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**(1st number + 1) × 3 = 2nd number**.

Now,

32 : 99

⇒ (32 + 1) × 3 → 33 × 3 = 99.

For, 16 : 51

⇒ (16 + 1) × 3 → 17 × 3 = 51.

Similarly, for ? : 45

⇒ (**14** + 1) × 3 → 15 × 3 = 45.

So, 14 : 45 is the related number.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question:
Which two digits need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

16 ÷ 7 × 2 + 4 − 3 = 12
questions.solution:
Given equation: 16 ÷ 7 × 2 + 4 − 3 = 12.

BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 2 and 4

Given: 16 ÷ 7 × 2 + 4 − 3 = 12

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**16 ÷ 7**__ × 4 + 2 − 3 = 12

⇒ __**2.29**____** × 4**__ + 2 − 3 = 12

⇒ __9.16 + 2__ - 3 = 12

⇒ __11.16 - 3__ = 12

⇒ 8.16 ≠ 12

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 2) 7 and 4**

Given: 16 ÷ 7 × 2 + 4 − 3 = 12

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**16 ÷ 4**__ × 2 + 7 − 3 = 12

⇒ __**4 × 2**__ + 7 − 3 = 12

⇒ __8 + 7__ – 3 = 12

⇒ __15____ – 3__ = 12

⇒ **12 = 12**

⇒ **LHS = RHS**

Option 3) 16 and 2

Given: 2 ÷ 7 × 16 + 4 − 3 = 12

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**2**____** ÷ 7**__ × 16 + 4 − 3 = 12

⇒ 0.29 × 16 + 4 − 3 = 12

⇒ __4.64__ + 4 – 3 = 12

⇒ __8.64 - 3__ = 12

⇒ 5.64 ≠ 12

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) 7 and 3

Given: 16 ÷ 7 × 2 + 4 − 3 = 12

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**16 ÷ 3**__ × 2 + 4 − 7 = 12

⇒ __**5.33**____** × 2**__ + 4 − 7 = 12

⇒ __10.66 + 4__ - 7 = 12

⇒ __14.66 - 7__ = 12

⇒ 7.66 ≠ 12

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Seven teachers M, N, O, P, Q, R and S take different number of tuitions. P takes more tuitions than S. M takes more tuitions than Q. R takes the second highest number of tuitions. The number of tuitions that O takes is less than only that of four teachers. N takes less tuitions than P but more than M. Q takes the least number of tuitions. S takes the second lowest number of tuitions.

In terms of the number of tuitions taken, who is between N and S?
questions.solution:
Given: Seven teachers M, N, O, P, Q, R and S.

1) Q takes the least number of tuitions.

2) S takes the second lowest number of tuitions.

3) R takes the second highest number of tuitions.

__ > R > __ > __ > __ > S > Q

4) O takes is less than only that of four teachers.

__ > R > __ > __ > O > S > Q

5) N takes less tuitions than P but more than M.

P > R > N > M > O > S > Q

So, M and O took tuitions between N and S.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(**NOTE :** Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(2, 3, 25)

(3, 4, 49)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**(1st number + 2nd number)² = 3rd number**.

Now,

(2, 3, 25)

⇒ (2 + 3)² → 5² = 25

For (3, 4, 49)

⇒ (3 + 4)2 → 72 = 49.

Now, checking the options:

**Option 1: (4, 5, 81)**

**⇒ (4 + 5)2 → 92 = 81.**

Option 2: (4, 5, 91)

⇒ (4 + 5)2 → 92 = 81 ≠ 91.

Option 3: (4, 6, 110)

⇒ (4 + 6)2 → 102 = 100 ≠ 110.

Option 4: (4, 7,111)

⇒ (4 + 7)2 → 112 = 121 ≠ 111.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some M are P.

II. All X are M.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some P are X.

II. Some P are M.

III. No P is X.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Statements:

I. Some M are P.

II. All X are M.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c924257f977cd132cf06f258a1f819a9ce684c25181510ce8b1b0868b09d4a2.png] 

Conclusions:

(i) Some P are X - False (Because no direct related given between P and X, so it can be possible not definite).

(ii) Some P are M - **True** (Because Some M are P, so some P are also M).

(III) No P is X - False (Because, negative conclusion can't be definitely true in positive statement).

Here, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
